sections.h2: Who handles property tax for a Menifee County house?
sections.html:
Three Frenchburg offices share the chores here. An elected appraiser, known as the PVA, values each house. The sheriff mails and takes in the bill. The clerk receives whatever remains unpaid when April 15 closes. Match your question to the right desk and a payoff figure or a corrected value comes faster.

The PVA, clerk and county attorney all list 12 Main Street on the county website, while the sheriff keeps a post office box of its own.

sections.h2: What is Menifee County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Menifee is mountain country, with roughly 204 square miles of land carved out on May 29, 1869 from Bath, Montgomery, Morgan, Powell and Wolfe counties. Frenchburg is both seat and sole city, and its charter dates to 1871 according to the county. Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge flank the county, and Lexington is under 70 miles away via the Mountain Parkway.

National forest land takes up much of Menifee, and cultivated farms cover about a tenth of it. Sellers here mostly offer hillside lots, small tracts and cabins. The county website names tourism, forestry, small business, farming and public service as the economy. Menifee belongs to the Mount Sterling micropolitan area, and the school district office is on Wynn Flat Road in Frenchburg.

A March 2, 2012 EF3 tornado cut through Menifee and neighboring counties, and three people were killed in the region. A lender may ask about storm repairs on an older house, so keep permits and receipts together.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Menifee County housing?
sections.html:
Menifee counted 6,113 residents in 2020, a dip from 6,306 a decade earlier, and a mid-2025 estimate of 6,430 would be a 5.2 percent bounce. The 2020 count tallied 3,277 housing units, 24.3 percent of them empty, and classed the entire county as rural.

The five year survey adds these points:

  • Owners live in 75.5 percent of the homes.
  • Monthly owner costs run $996 with a mortgage and $299 without one.
  • Broadband reaches 81.2 percent of households, so ask what internet a remote address can get.
  • A worker's average trip to the job takes 29.8 minutes.
  • Per capita income is $25,879, and covered employment was just 454 jobs in 2023, up 3.9 percent from a year earlier.

sections.h2: Which Menifee County offices should you contact?
sections.html:
Every office keeps its own mailing box, so double check the address before anything goes in the mail.

  • Sheriff: collects the bills. P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, (606) 768-3875.
  • PVA: values, exemption forms and conferences. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 36, (606) 768-3514.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and the desk where appeals are filed. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 123, (606) 768-3512.
  • County Attorney: delinquent bill notices and payment plans. 12 Main Street, P.O. Box 545, (606) 768-2606.

Call ahead for office hours before you drive in.

sections.h2: What are the Menifee County payment deadlines?
sections.html:
The sheriff runs the statewide calendar found in KRS 134.015. Bills arrive in the fall and follow whoever held title on January 1.

  • Through November 1: pay 2 percent less.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the bill as printed.
  • During January: 5 percent extra.
  • February 1 to April 15: the state shows a 21 percent combined penalty.
  • After April 15: the clerk holds it.

A house sold later in the year still carries the earlier owner's name on that year's bill. Settle the split in the contract and ask the sheriff for the balance.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Menifee County property value?
sections.html:
Sit down with the PVA first, and go to the clerk only if the two of you cannot agree. Inspection starts on the first Monday in May and lasts two weeks, and filing closes one workday later.

A local board then hears the case within 25 to 35 days and gets five sitting days without state permission. Revenue officials say a claim without evidence must be denied, so bring paper.

  • Photos and contractor quotes for a worn roof or a shifting foundation on a slope.
  • Prices that comparable houses nearby fetched this past year.
  • Insurance policies or construction costs.

Audio recording of the hearing is allowed. A paid representative must belong to a group listed in KRS 133.120 and carry your signed authorization.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead break for Menifee County seniors?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners aged 65 or older and for those classified as totally disabled. File at the Menifee County PVA for the house you occupy. Each residential unit gets just one exemption under KRS 132.810, and manufactured homes qualify as units.

The exempt amount tracks a federal price index, so ask the PVA for today's figure. An approval granted after you paid brings a refund on the exempt slice. A sale or a death must be reported, and whoever takes the house files anew.

sections.h2: What happens when a Menifee County bill is not paid?
sections.html:
When April 15 ends, the sheriff passes the bill to the clerk and a lien goes on record. Interest starts at 1 percent each month, with a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent county attorney charge on top. The clerk may sell the certificate to an outside investor from mid-July onward.

The county attorney can arrange installments before a sale. Afterward you answer to the investor, who may add large fees. Under the statute the January 1 owner owes the tax personally, and the lien can ride with the parcel for 11 years.

sections.h2: How are cabins and short-term rentals taxed in Menifee County?
sections.html:
A 4 percent transient tax applies to short-term rentals, and the county's Departments page links the registration form and the monthly return. With Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge nearby, plenty of cabins fit that description.

A buyer who plans to rent will want those filings in order. If you hosted guests, gather your returns and tell the buyer what you filed. The county tourism office on that page can explain how a new owner registers.

sections.h2: Can a Menifee County house with tax owing still be sold?
sections.html:
Yes. An open bill, or one already at the clerk, turns into a payoff number that the sheriff or clerk will quote. Once the bill is at the clerk the number climbs monthly, so it is worth getting a fresh quote close to closing.

Homes here are often inherited, remote or in need of work. The median household income of $45,096 is the lowest among the four counties in the Census table, and 23.6 percent of residents live below the poverty line. To compare a listing with a cash offer, subtract repairs, carrying costs and back tax from each. Get the payoff in writing before you accept anything.

faqs.q: Whom do I pay for Menifee County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Menifee County Sheriff at P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875. Write the bill number on a mailed payment.

faqs.q: Which date ends the penalty-free window in Menifee County?
faqs.a: December 31. A bill paid by then costs its printed amount, and January adds 5 percent.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed in Menifee County?
faqs.a: At the county clerk's office, after a conference with the PVA. The filing is due one workday after the May inspection period ends.

faqs.q: Does Menifee County give older owners a tax break?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Kentucky homestead exemption for owners 65 or older who live in the house. Apply at the PVA, 12 Main Street in Frenchburg.

faqs.q: Can the county take a house over a small unpaid bill?
faqs.a: After April 15 a lien is recorded, and collection may include selling the certificate to a private buyer. Speak with the county attorney early about installments.
